I am a postdoctoral researcher at Arizona State University working at the intersection of semiconductor systems, artificial intelligence, digital twins, and hardware/software co-design. My research focuses on how deployed semiconductor systems can remain reliable, explainable, and resilient as workloads, software, environments, and devices change over time.

My current work develops AI-enabled methods for Silicon Lifecycle Management (SLM), including runtime telemetry analytics, lightweight digital twins, explainable anomaly detection, causal diagnosis, uncertainty-aware decision support, and edge and on-chip deployment. A central goal is to move semiconductor monitoring beyond simple detect-and-notify workflows toward measure-explain-act lifecycle intelligence.

## Biography

In 2020, I moved to Arizona to begin my M.S. program in Robotics and Autonomous Systems, with a concentration in Systems Engineering, at Arizona State University's School of Manufacturing Systems and Networks. I earned my master's degree in 2022 and completed my Ph.D. in Systems Engineering in 2025 under Dr. Oswald Chong.

My doctoral research focused on AI-driven system optimization for semiconductor manufacturing facilities. I studied mechanical, electrical, and plumbing systems in high-reliability fab environments, with applications in predictive modeling, energy efficiency, indoor air quality, and supply-chain resilience. This work helped me see semiconductor manufacturing as a complex engineered system that must remain efficient, reliable, and resilient under uncertainty.

I am currently a Postdoctoral Researcher under Dr. Krishnendu Chakrabarty at ASU. My postdoctoral research focuses on AI-enabled lifecycle intelligence for semiconductor systems, especially Silicon Lifecycle Management, telemetry-driven digital twins, explainable anomaly detection, and hardware/software co-design.

## Research Interests

- Silicon Lifecycle Management and dependable computing: runtime telemetry, in-field monitoring, anomaly detection, diagnosis, and guarded response.
- Hardware/software co-design for edge and on-chip AI: fixed-point anomaly scoring, feature-budgeted telemetry analytics, area/power-aware deployment, and near-device decision support.
- Digital twins and telemetry-driven modeling: behavioral micro-twins, tiered observability, split-conformal calibration, and host-side monitoring under limited signal access.
- Causal and explainable telemetry analytics: causal graph learning, feature ranking, signal-level attribution, and engineer-trustworthy diagnosis.
- Semiconductor manufacturing facility intelligence: AI-driven HVAC/MEP optimization, energy efficiency, indoor air quality, reliability, supply-chain resilience, and circularity.
- Methods: time-series modeling, graph neural networks, multimodal AI, uncertainty-aware forecasting, Optuna-TPE, explainable AI, lightweight RAG/LLM-assisted triage, and rigorous evaluation.
